questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I primarily chose to apply to Glasgow University due to my wish to explore Scotland's nature

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Scottish nature and outdoor opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I just paid attention to my email both at KU and at Glasgow. However, I found the enrollment process quite stressful, since Glasgow University where short on staff, which made the repsonse time quite long

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really receive any assistance. I had to seek out a lot of information myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied early on, in start July. I went on different onlines sites such as Spareroom, through which I found my accomodation. My advice would be to start early, and put in an effort when writing to the subletters

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Glasgow is quite expensive and sits a lower housing standard. I think this is good to know it advance, but once your are there, you quicly get used to it

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing available through the university was very expensive and way off my budget.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think you just need to pay attention to the information you get via your email. It can be quite stressful, but there is no need to drive yourself crazy over it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the first week I went for my visa registration on campus. Afterwards I finallised my course-wish list. But I did not end up getting any of the courses I initially applied for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was hardly any help available in person. I contacted the exchange supervisor a couple of times, but I had to wait almost 5 days between answers, which was very irritating

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As I mentioned, I did not get any of the courses I wanted. It was only when I actually arrived in Glasgow that I was able to see the University's final course catalogue.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get too stressed about the long registration process, and long waiting time. Prepare yourself for the possibility that you will not get any of the courses you have planned for

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I would say there is a bit more reading for the different sessions. I did not have any lectures but only seminars. 

I would say the academic level was a bit lower than at UK, but I did not really mind it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No lectures, only seminars. More groupwork than at KU. Also there are midterms exams, and the semester is only 10 weeks. So all in all, more intense than a semester at KU

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Cognition - How Do We Know What We Know?

Ways of Living - Studying Others

Aftermath of Atrocity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the two last courses. The first was an introductory course to anthropology, but it was nice to dive into some classic texts and get presented with new terms and theories. Aftermath of Atrocity was very interesting course; it dealt with how societies and groups of people move on, find justice and reconciliation after atrocities such as mass genocide, ecocide, civil wars etc. The lecturer used a lot of anthropological documentaries, photos and so on the compliment the teaching

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had prepared to a lot of trips to the Scottish Highlands, which can be quite expensive due to trains, transport, accomodation. In that light, I did not really have any unexpected costs during my semester. But I will note, that groceries and eating out in Scotland is a lot cheaper than in Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and eating out was less expensive. Everything else was more or less the same as in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is lot of clubs, sportclubs and different student societies to join. I joined the walking society, which was a nice way to get out of the city and go on different treks with other students from the university

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sport activites were available. I did not join a whole lot, because I wanted to focus more on my trips to the Highlands and around Scotland

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join the walking society. 

Make sure to get out the city, the highlands and Scotland is very beautiful. One trip is NOT enough

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Isle of Skye 

Moffat-region. Stay overnight in a bothy (the scottish version of a danish 'shelter')

Oban - cute fishing village on the west coast 

Loch Lomond - beautiful plays for days trips out of Glasgow 

Inverness - capital of the Highlands 

Visit Edinburgh - a whole other vibe and city than Glasgow, so it is nice to see and experience the difference between these two cities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy. Scots are very friendly and welcoming

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do not worry about your english-level, you will get by just fine.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really encounter and challenging cultural differences. Scottish youth culture seems to be fairly similar to the Danish

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmness and friendly vibes of the scots.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Visit the Highlands 
Do not expect to get the courses you initially want 
Do not worry about your level of english

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Give yourself time and space to adjust to your new surroundings. Go explore Glasgow and Scotland

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring the Highlands and the smaller cities in Scotland

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling in a new and foreign city on your own. But accomplising this is also very empowering

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
